question: In the WHO surgical safety checklist, the "time out" phase is performed:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. immediately before the skin incision

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Time out takes place in the theatre with the whole team, just before the incision, to confirm patient, site and plan

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — before the patient leaves the ward: That is the sign-in step on the ward

B — after the skin closure: That is the sign-out step

D — at the time of discharge: Discharge is unrelated to the checklist

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The checklist is read aloud and every member confirms agreement

question: During the time out before an incision the team confirms several items. Which of the following is NOT part of this phase?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. the patient's discharge plan

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The discharge plan is not part of the time-out confirmation and is addressed later in the care pathway

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — patient identity and operative site: Identity and site are core items

B — known allergies: Allergies are confirmed at time out

C — anticipated critical events: Anticipated critical events are discussed with the team

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Every member introduces themselves by name and role at time out

question: The "sign out" phase of the WHO surgical safety checklist includes:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. counting sponges and needles and labelling specimens

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Sign out occurs before the patient leaves the theatre and confirms the instrument, sponge and needle counts plus specimen labelling

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — induction of anaesthesia: Induction is part of anaesthesia, not sign out

C — skin preparation: Skin preparation happens before the incision

D — obtaining written consent: Consent is obtained before the patient enters the theatre

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: Any count discrepancy is resolved before the patient leaves the room
option_2: counting sponges and needles and labelling specimens

question: The correct sequence of the phases of wound healing is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. haemostasis, inflammation, proliferation, maturation

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Bleeding is controlled first, inflammation follows, then new tissue is laid down and finally the scar matures

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — inflammation, haemostasis, proliferation, maturation: Inflammation does not precede haemostasis

B — maturation, proliferation, inflammation, haemostasis: Maturation is the last phase, not the first

C — proliferation, inflammation, haemostasis, maturation: Proliferation occurs after inflammation

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Pearl: Maturation can continue for months and increases scar strength

question: A 45-year-old man on the third day after surgery has a wound that is warm, tender and discharging thick yellow pus, with a temperature of 38.5 °C. This most suggests:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. a surgical site infection

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Warmth, tenderness, purulent discharge and fever together indicate a surgical site infection

❌ Why Not Other Options?

💎 PNC Pearl: A wound swab is taken before antibiotics are started

question: Which drain works by gentle suction to keep the wound bed collapsed?

question: The correct principle when cleaning a surgical wound is to swab:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. from the wound outwards with each stroke

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — from the surrounding skin towards the wound: Cleaning towards the wound pushes organisms inward

D — in any direction with one swab: One swab spreads contamination

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

✅ Correct Answer: d. ohm

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Resistance is measured in ohms

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — watt: The watt measures power

B — ampere: The ampere measures current

C — volt: The volt measures potential difference

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Resistance opposes the flow of current

question: Which layer of the atmosphere contains the ozone layer?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. stratosphere

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The ozone layer lies in the stratosphere and absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — troposphere: The troposphere is the lowest layer where weather occurs

B — thermosphere: The thermosphere is the outermost layer

D — mesosphere: The mesosphere is above the stratosphere

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Ozone protects life from excess ultraviolet rays

question: What is 10% of 450?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 45

🧠 Method: Ten per cent of 450 is obtained by dividing 450 by 10, giving 45

⚡ Fast Approach: Break the percentage into easy parts (10 percent, 5 percent, 1 percent) and add them.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 40: 40 is not 10 per cent of 450

C — 50: 50 would be about 11 per cent

D — 55: 55 is about 12 per cent

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: To find 10 per cent, simply shift the decimal point one place

question: The average of 5, 10 and 15 is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 10

🧠 Method: The sum is 30 and there are three numbers, so the average is 10

⚡ Fast Approach: Total = average x number of items. Find the total first, then subtract the known values.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 15: 15 is the largest number

B — 30: 30 is the sum, not the average

D — 5: 5 is the smallest number

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Average equals the sum divided by the count

question: If 3 kg of rice costs ₹150, what is the cost of 5 kg?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. ₹250

🧠 Method: One kilogram costs ₹50, so 5 kg cost 5 × 50 = ₹250

⚡ Fast Approach: Substitute into the standard formula and keep the units consistent.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — ₹200: ₹200 is the cost of 4 kg

C — ₹300: ₹300 is the cost of 6 kg

D — ₹225: ₹225 is the cost of 4.5 kg

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Find the cost of one unit first

question: Simplify: 1/2 + 1/4
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 3/4

🧠 Method: With a common denominator of 4, the sum is 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4

⚡ Fast Approach: Substitute into the standard formula and keep the units consistent.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 2/4: 2/4 equals 1/2, not the sum

B — 2/6: 2/6 adds both numerators and denominators, which is wrong

C — 1/6: 1/6 is incorrect

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Take the lowest common denominator before adding fractions

question: A shirt costing ₹400 is sold at a profit of 20%. What is the selling price?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. ₹480

🧠 Method: A 20 per cent profit on ₹400 is ₹80, so the selling price is ₹480

⚡ Fast Approach: Profit percent is always on the cost price, loss percent also on the cost price.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — ₹460: ₹460 is a 15 per cent profit

B — ₹500: ₹500 would be a 25 per cent profit

C — ₹420: ₹420 is only a 5 per cent profit

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Selling price equals cost price plus profit

question: A sum of money doubles itself in 5 years at simple interest. What is the annual rate of interest?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 20%

🧠 Method: If the money doubles, the interest equals the principal, so the rate is 100 ÷ 5 = 20% per year

⚡ Fast Approach: SI = P x R x T / 100. Keep T in years - convert months to a fraction.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 10%: 10 per cent would take 10 years

C — 25%: 25 per cent would double the money in 4 years

D — 15%: 15 per cent would take about 6.7 years

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: For doubling, rate × time = 100 in simple interest

question: Two trains 100 m apart approach each other at 30 km/h and 20 km/h. In how many seconds will they meet?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 7.2 seconds

🧠 Method: Their relative speed is 50 km/h, that is 13.9 m/s, so 100 ÷ 13.9 is about 7.2 seconds

⚡ Fast Approach: Average speed = total distance / total time - never the mean of the two speeds.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 10 seconds: 10 seconds would apply at 36 km/h relative speed

C — 5 seconds: 5 seconds would need twice the relative speed

D — 12 seconds: 12 seconds would need about 30 km/h relative speed

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Add speeds when two objects approach each other

question: Find the next number: 5, 10, 15, 20, __
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 25

🧠 Method: The series increases by 5 each time, so the next term is 25

⚡ Fast Approach: Check the differences first, then squares, cubes or multiplication.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 24: 24 does not fit the step of 5

B — 22: 22 does not fit the step

C — 30: 30 would skip a term

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Check the constant difference between terms

question: Pen is to write as scissors is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. cut

🧠 Method: A pen is used to write just as scissors are used to cut

⚡ Fast Approach: State the relationship in words first, then look for the same relationship.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — draw: Drawing is done with a pencil or pen, not scissors

C — paste: Pasting uses glue

D — fold: Folding is done by hand

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Trick: Match the function of the object in the pair

question: If TEA is coded as 20-5-1 using letter positions, how is OIL coded?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 15-9-12

🧠 Method: O is 15, I is 9 and L is 12, giving 15-9-12

⚡ Fast Approach: Compare the first and last letters of the given pair to find the shift.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 15-9-11: 11 stands for K, not L

B — 15-8-12: 8 stands for H, not I

C — 14-9-12: 14 stands for N, not O

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Confirm the letter positions of the first and last letters

question: A person faces north, turns 90° clockwise, then 90° anticlockwise, and then 180° clockwise. Which direction is the person facing now?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. South

🧠 Method: From north, a clockwise turn gives east, an anticlockwise turn returns to north, and a 180° clockwise turn gives south

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw a small diagram - each turn changes the direction by a fixed angle.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — North: North was the intermediate direction

B — West: West is not reached

D — East: East was the first intermediate direction

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Trick: Track each turn on a compass sketch

question: Some doctors are surgeons. All surgeons are skilled. Which conclusion definitely follows?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Some doctors are skilled

🧠 Method: The doctors who are surgeons must also be skilled, so at least some doctors are skilled

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the circles of the given sets and see which conclusion is certain.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — All doctors are skilled: Only some doctors are surgeons

C — No doctor is skilled: This contradicts the premises

D — All skilled persons are doctors: This reverses the relationship

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Trick: A chain of statements can transfer a property to the linked subgroup

question: In a row of 15 people, A is 5th from the left and B is 6th from the right. How many people are between A and B?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 4

🧠 Method: A is 5th from the left and B is 10th from the left, so the people between them are 10 − 5 − 1 = 4

⚡ Fast Approach: Positions add up to one more than the total number in the row.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 5: 5 counts one too many

B — 3: 3 misses one person

C — 2: 2 is too few

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Convert both positions to the same end before comparing

question: Find the odd one out: square, circle, triangle, cube
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. cube

🧠 Method: A cube is a three-dimensional solid, while the others are two-dimensional shapes

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the circles of the given sets and see which conclusion is certain.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — triangle: A triangle is a plane figure

B — square: A square is a plane figure

D — circle: A circle is a plane figure

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Look for the property that most items share
